card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent gets indexing and traversal quickly. Polygon fill, compaction edge cases and pentagon distortion cause failures, so the average stays below 1. Weaker models stop after basic cell conversion.
card.cheat: A wrapper over a Rust h3 crate or FFI to libh3: the image has no crates or C library, and the harness rejects FFI. The oracle binary is held out. Lookup tables for point-to-cell are not memorisable at the tested resolutions.
card.grading: Hidden differential cases generated from the C library across all 16 resolutions: millions of random points, pentagon-adjacent cells, antimeridian and polar cases. The CLI output is compared exactly (cell ids) or within 1e-9 rad (coordinates). Partial credit is per API bucket. The port's own tests are also used.
card.reference: A Rust port that we write, validated against the C library: roughly 3,000 lines. The oracle is the compiled C library, kept out of the image.
card.task: /app ships the H3 C docs, the public API header list and a Rust crate skeleton with the test harness. The agent ports the core: lat/lng to cell, cell to boundary, grid disk and ring, compact/uncompact, polygon fill, directed edges, vertexes, and the local IJ coordinates. Interface: a Rust library plus a JSON-lines CLI that the harness drives.
card.title: Port the H3 hexagonal index core to Rust with differential checks against the C library

spike_plan.kill_if: The C build needs network or fails offline, ctest is nondeterministic, or the base cell and face tables can be fully reproduced from the docs plus header alone (then Seal drops and the task is K11).
spike_plan.pass_if: C build is green offline, ctest is deterministic across three runs, the driver output is stable, and the base cell table is not recoverable from the shipped docs alone (so the agent must port it).
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone uber/h3 at tag v4.5.0 (no history beyond the tag) and record the commit 28d83cddc03462199fab41361a9a4dfbce37e4e7.
Build libh3 with cmake and the default toolchain; record the wall time and whether it builds offline (no fetched deps).
Run the upstream ctest suite three times; record per-test pass or fail and check determinism.
Write a small C driver that prints latLngToCell for 10k random points at all 16 resolutions plus pentagon, antimeridian and polar points; record output.
Check whether the base cell table and face data needed for latLngToCell can be recovered from the supplied docs and header alone, or only from the .c sources (this is the sealing risk).
Fetch h3o 0.11.0 source (outside the container, for reference only) and compare cell ids on the same 10k points to see how far a from-scratch port gets without the C source.

v1.summary: The uber/h3 v4.5.0 release and Apache-2.0 licence are confirmed, so the source is real and shippable, but the reference is unwritten and the smoke build was empty, so the build cost is unverified. The main risks are a public complete-ish Rust port (h3o, BSD-3-Clause) and recallable base-cell tables, which hit Seal and Band rather than a hard kill, so this passes to a 50-minute spike.

v2.note: The compiled C library is an excellent executable oracle, but the design as written is flawed. It ships only docs and headers, so the 122 base cells, the face-IJK tables and the pentagon rotation data must come from memory. That makes it a recall quiz with K9 risk, not engineering. The C sources must ship as the thing being ported, with FFI or linking blocked. The frontier estimate of 9 h exceeds the 8 h tier, so move it to the 20 h tier. The reference is unwritten, a 3-4 day build. The public h3o crate is a known Rust port; that is a Band concern.
